Porting of [core/composables/settings.composable.ts]: keeps the URL from the server [NestJS] in memory.

// =========================================================================
// core/services/settings_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/composables/settings.composable.ts (Vue.js client of this
// course): a tiny "store" that keeps the server's URL in memory
// NestJS.
//
// Vue.js exposes this shared state via the pair [provide]/[inject]: an
// [reactive(...)] object created once, then read/modified in place
// by any descendant component. Flutter has neither [reactive] nor
// [provide]/[inject]: the standard equivalent in the ecosystem (and the one
// used in this course) is a ChangeNotifier—a regular Dart class
// that, in addition to its fields, knows PRÉVENIR its listeners
// whenever a change requires a new display, via
// an explicit call to notifyListeners().
//
// The key difference from Vue.js: [reactive(...)] wraps the object
// in a proxy JavaScript that detects AUTOMATIQUEMENT every time the
// property (store.apiBaseUrl = ... automatically redraws the components that
// read apiBaseUrl). A Dart ChangeNotifier, on the other hand, does not detect RIEN at all
// on its own: it’s up to the developer to call notifyListeners() after every
// change—a little more manual discipline in exchange for a
// much simpler mechanism (no proxy, no “magic”) that’s
// understand and debug.
//
// It is the [provider] package (see pubspec.yaml and lib/main.dart) that plays
// Next, regarding this ChangeNotifier, the role of app.provide(...) on the
// Vue.js: it makes this unique instance available to the entire sub-tree of
// widgets, via context.watch<SettingsService>() (to “read and
// resubscribe to changes," see lib/app.dart) or context.read<...>()
// (to "read once, without resubscribing").
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

class SettingsService extends ChangeNotifier {
  String _apiBaseUrl = 'http://localhost:8080';

  String get apiBaseUrl => _apiBaseUrl;

  // equivalent to "setApiBaseUrl(url: string)" on the Vue.js side—unlike
  // from store.apiBaseUrl = url (a simple assignment, sufficient thanks to the
  // responsive proxy), here we must explicitly notify listeners after
  // changing the private field.
  void setApiBaseUrl(String url) {
    if (url == _apiBaseUrl) {
      return; // prevents unnecessary redrawing if the value has not actually changed
    }
    _apiBaseUrl = url;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 36–39: [class SettingsService extends ChangeNotifier] with a field PRIVÉ ([_apiBaseUrl]) and a public accessor ([get apiBaseUrl]) — a [ChangeNotifier] is a [Dart] ORDINAIRE class, with no proxy such as [reactive(...)] on the [Vue.js] side: nothing automatically detects a property read or write.
  • Lines 45–51: [setApiBaseUrl(url)] explicitly calls [notifyListeners()] and APRÈS to update the field — the manual step that [store.apiBaseUrl = url] did not need to perform on the [Vue.js] side, since the reactive proxy handles it on its own.

docs.title: 5.6.2. lib/core/services/auth_service.dart
docs.text:
Porting of [core/composables/auth.composable.ts]: manages the connection (POST [/login]), maintains the token [JWT], and ensures it survives a restart via [shared_preferences].

// =========================================================================
// core/services/auth_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/composables/auth.composable.ts (Vue.js client of this
// session): manages the user’s connection, calls POST /login, stores
// the received token JWT (and the accompanying identity/role), and ensures that it
// survive an application restart thanks to shared_preferences—
// the cross-platform equivalent of localStorage (see below).
//
// Like Vue.js, this is the only other place in the application, along with
// core/services/rdv_service.dart, which communicates with the server using HTTP—an
// is an assumed exception to the rule “only one place that communicates with the server using HTTP,” which
// reflects, on the client side, the separation already made on the server side between
// RdvMedecinsController (business logic) and AuthController (authentication).
//
// DIFFÉRENCE IMPORTANTE with Vue.js: lireSessionStockee() (on the Vue.js side)
// is SYNCHRONE—localStorage.getItem(...) returns its value
// immediately, even before the application is rendered for the first time. shared_
// preferences, on the other hand, is asynchronous (TOUJOURS asynchrone (SharedPreferences.getInstance()
// returns a Future), even on platforms where the underlying storage
// is actually a local file that can be read almost instantly: the API Dart does not
// does not distinguish between these cases, to ensure consistency across TOUTES platforms (on
// the web, this same call relies on window.localStorage, but the API Dart
// remains asynchronous to ensure consistency with other targets). As a result
// : unlike on the Vue.js side, we can no longer read the session that has already been
// stored in AVANT during widget tree construction—a [init()]
// explicitly asynchronous, called (and ATTENDU with `await`) from
// lib/main.dart before runApp(...), to prevent the login screen from
// "flickers" for a fraction of a second before the session is restored.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import '../models/rdv_models.dart';
import 'settings_service.dart';

const String _cleStockage = 'rdvmedecins.session';

class AuthService extends ChangeNotifier {
  // passed to the constructor rather than obtained via Flutter injection: at this
  // stage (see lib/main.dart), no widgets exist yet, so nothing
  // such as context.read<SettingsService>() would be possible—exactly
  // the same reason as the one documented in creerAuthStore(settings) on the
  // Vue.js (src/main.ts), which also receives settingsStore as a function parameter
  // via a function call rather than through inject().
  final SettingsService settings;

  AuthService(this.settings);

  bool estConnecte = false;
  String? login;
  String? nom;
  Role? role;
  String? accessToken;

  bool get estAdmin => role == Role.admin;

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // to call UNE SEULE times, in lib/main.dart, AVANT runApp(...): re-reads
  // any session already saved during a previous launch of
  // the application—equivalent to lireSessionStockee() on the Vue.js side, but
  // explicitly asynchronous (see the header of this file) rather than called
  // within the store’s constructor itself.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> init() async {
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      final brut = prefs.getString(_cleStockage);
      if (brut == null) {
        return; // no session stored: remains “not logged in,” default values as above
      }
      final session = jsonDecode(brut) as Map<String, dynamic>;
      _appliquerSessionLocale(
        accessToken: session['accessToken'] as String,
        login: session['login'] as String,
        nom: session['nom'] as String,
        role: Role.depuisChaine(session['role'] as String),
      );
    } catch (_) {
      // shared_preferences may be unavailable or contain a
      // corrupted value—in this case, as shown on the Vue.js side (try/catch block of
      // lireSessionStockee()), we simply assume that there is no
      // session, rather than causing the application to crash on startup.
    }
    // no notifyListeners() here: init() is awaited before
    // runApp(...) in lib/main.dart, so no widget is listening to this
    // ChangeNotifier at the time this method executes—notifying it would
    // would serve no purpose (and would even throw an exception, a ChangeNotifier
    // Flutter prohibits calling notifyListeners() before having at least one
    // listener in certain debug configurations).
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: POST /login body JSON { login, password }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<LoginResultat> seConnecter(String login, String password) async {
    final reponseHttp = await http.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/login'),
      headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
      body: jsonEncode({'login': login, 'password': password}),
    );
    final enveloppe = Reponse<LoginResultat>.fromJson(
      jsonDecode(reponseHttp.body) as Map<String, dynamic>,
      (donnees) => LoginResultat.fromJson(donnees as Map<String, dynamic>),
    );
    if (enveloppe.status != 0 || enveloppe.data == null) {
      throw Exception('Échec de connexion');
    }
    final resultat = enveloppe.data!;
    await _appliquerSessionEtPersister(resultat);
    return resultat;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // logout: purely local (no server call—a JWT token is not
  // "revokes" on the server side in this port; it expires on its own after
  // JWT_EXPIRES_IN, see the .env server). Called either by clicking
  // "Log Out" (see lib/app.dart) or by core/http/auth_http_client.dart
  // when a protected request receives a 401 response.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> seDeconnecter() async {
    login = null;
    nom = null;
    role = null;
    accessToken = null;
    estConnecte = false;
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.remove(_cleStockage);
    } catch (_) {
      // Again, a failure to clear the storage should not prevent the
      // the application-side disconnection, which has already taken effect above.
    }
  }

  // updates the reactive fields SANS that interact with storage—used by
  // init() (which actually comes from DE LIRE the storage; no need to rewrite it).
  void _appliquerSessionLocale({
    required String accessToken,
    required String login,
    required String nom,
    required Role role,
  }) {
    this.accessToken = accessToken;
    this.login = login;
    this.nom = nom;
    this.role = role;
    estConnecte = true;
  }

  // updates the reactive fields ET persists the session—used by
  // seConnecter() above. Combines what appliquerSession(...) did
  // into a single block on the Vue.js side (reactive state + localStorage writes
  // together); here, the two operations are separated because the write
  // is asynchronous (await prefs.setString(...)) whereas the update
  // of the fields must be performed IMMÉDIATEMENT synchronously
  // (notifyListeners() must follow the field assignment without waiting for
  // disk I/O)—reversing the order would unnecessarily delay the refresh
  // of the interface.
  Future<void> _appliquerSessionEtPersister(LoginResultat resultat) async {
    _appliquerSessionLocale(
      accessToken: resultat.accessToken,
      login: resultat.login,
      nom: resultat.nom,
      role: resultat.role,
    );
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.setString(
        _cleStockage,
        jsonEncode({
          'accessToken': resultat.accessToken,
          'login': resultat.login,
          'nom': resultat.nom,
          'role': resultat.role.versChaine(),
        }),
      );
    } catch (_) {
      // The session remains valid EN MÉMOIRE for this execution of
      // the application, even if persistence fails (quota exceeded,
      // read-only storage...)—only a future restart of
      // the application would be affected (the user would have to log in again).
    }
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 16–29: The header comment details the most significant difference in this file—[lireSessionStockee()] on the [Vue.js] side is SYNCHRONE; [shared_preferences] is asynchronous relative to TOUJOURS, regardless of the platform, hence an explicit [init()] relative to [async], which is expected by [lib/main.dart], AVANT, and [runApp(...)].
  • lines 69–95: [Future<void> init() async { ... }] — reads any cached session, protected by a [try/catch] — same precaution as for [try/catch] from [lireSessionStockee()] on the [Vue.js] side (storage unavailable or value corrupted).
  • lines 100–116: [seConnecter(login, password)] — calls POST [/login] with the package [http] (the equivalent of [fetch]), throws a standard [Dart] exception ([throw Exception(...)]) in case of failure—which is later intercepted by a [try/catch] [Dart], just as the [throw new Error(...)] from [auth.composable.ts] was intercepted by a [.catch(...)] [JavaScript].
  • lines 165–190: [_appliquerSessionEtPersister(...)] — updates the fields; ET calls [notifyListeners()] and AVANT to write to [shared_preferences]: The order is arbitrary—the interface must refresh IMMÉDIATEMENT without waiting for an asynchronous disk write, whereas [appliquerSession(...)] on the [Vue.js] side performed both operations in a single synchronous instruction.

docs.text:
Port of [core/services/rdv.service.ts]: the five business logic calls to the server, built on top of [core/http/auth_http_client.dart] (below) rather than directly on the [http] package.

// =========================================================================
// core/services/rdv_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Porting core/services/rdv.service.ts (the Vue.js client from this course): the
// the [Services] layer of the Flutter client—the SEUL location of the application
// (with core/services/auth_service.dart for the connection itself), which
// communicates with the server NestJS via HTTP.
//
// Vue.js exposes this service as a COMPOSABLE (useRdvService()), which itself
// built on top of two other composables (useAuthFetch(), useSettings()).
// Since Flutter/Dart has neither composables nor built-in dependency injection
// in the language, this file reverts to a standard CLASSE, built
// once in lib/main.dart with its two dependencies passed to the
// constructor—exactly the same principle as core/http/auth_http_client.dart,
//, and the most direct way to port “a set of functions that
// depend on something else" when the target language does not offer composables.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../http/auth_http_client.dart';
import '../models/rdv_models.dart';
import 'settings_service.dart';

class RdvService {
  final AuthHttpClient authHttp;
  final SettingsService settings;

  RdvService(this.authHttp, this.settings);

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // shared private function: all server responses take the form
  // { status, data } (see core/models/rdv_models.dart). We centralize ICI,
  // once, applying the rule “if status != 0, it’s an error” rather
  // than repeating it in each of the methods below—exactly the
  // role of extracting<T>(...) on the Vue.js side.
  //
  // [parseData] is the same type of parameter as the one already encountered
  // in Reponse.fromJson(...) (see rdv_models.dart): the function that knows
  // to reconstruct a T from the raw JSON in the [data] field, since Dart
  // cannot do this on its own (no generic "T.fromJson(...)").
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  T _extraire<T>(http.Response reponseHttp, T Function(dynamic donneesBrutes) parseData) {
    final enveloppe = Reponse<T>.fromJson(
      jsonDecode(reponseHttp.body) as Map<String, dynamic>,
      parseData,
    );
    if (enveloppe.status != 0) {
      // we convert the server’s “business” error into a standard Dart
      // that the calling widgets can catch with a
      // simple try/catch (see lib/app.dart)—exactly like the
      // "throw new Error(...)" in rdv.service.ts, intercepted by the
      // .catch(...) in src/app/App.vue.
      throw Exception("Le serveur a répondu avec le statut d'erreur ${enveloppe.status}");
    }
    return enveloppe.data as T;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: GET /getAllMedecins
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<List<Medecin>> getAllMedecins() async {
    final reponseHttp = await authHttp.get(Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getAllMedecins'));
    return _extraire<List<Medecin>>(
      reponseHttp,
      (donnees) => (donnees as List<dynamic>).map((e) => Medecin.fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList(),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: GET /getAllClients
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<List<Client>> getAllClients() async {
    final reponseHttp = await authHttp.get(Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getAllClients'));
    return _extraire<List<Client>>(
      reponseHttp,
      (donnees) => (donnees as List<dynamic>).map((e) => Client.fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList(),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: GET /getAgendaMedecinJour/{idMedecin}/{day}
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<AgendaMedecinJour> getAgendaMedecinJour(int idMedecin, String jour) async {
    final reponseHttp = await authHttp.get(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getAgendaMedecinJour/$idMedecin/$jour'),
    );
    return _extraire<AgendaMedecinJour>(
      reponseHttp,
      (donnees) => AgendaMedecinJour.fromJson(donnees as Map<String, dynamic>),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: POST /ajouterRv body JSON { day, idClient, idCreneau }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<RvJson> ajouterRv(String jour, int idClient, int idCreneau) async {
    final reponseHttp = await authHttp.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/ajouterRv'),
      body: jsonEncode({'jour': jour, 'idClient': idClient, 'idCreneau': idCreneau}),
    );
    return _extraire<RvJson>(reponseHttp, (donnees) => RvJson.fromJson(donnees as Map<String, dynamic>));
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: POST /supprimerRv body JSON { idRv }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> supprimerRv(int idRv) async {
    final reponseHttp = await authHttp.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/supprimerRv'),
      body: jsonEncode({'idRv': idRv}),
    );
    _extraire<Object?>(reponseHttp, (donnees) => donnees);
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 27–31: [class RdvService { final AuthHttpClient authHttp; final SettingsService settings; RdvService(this.authHttp, this.settings); }] — reverts to a CLASSE ORDINAIRE, constructed once in [lib/main.dart] with its dependencies passed to the constructor, whereas [Vue.js] used COMPOSABLE and [useRdvService()], which were themselves built from two other composables.
  • Lines 45–59: [T _extraire<T>(reponseHttp, parseData)]—centralizes, just once, the rule “if [status != 0], it’s an error,” exactly the role of [extraire<T>(...)] relative to [Vue.js]—the parameter [parseData] is the same type of function already encountered in [Reponse.fromJson(...)].
  • Lines 99–105: [ajouterRv(jour, idClient, idCreneau)] — [jsonEncode({...})] constructs the body JSON of the request POST, the equivalent [Dart] of [JSON.stringify({...})] on the [Vue.js] side.
  • Lines 110–116: [Future<void> supprimerRv(int idRv) async { ... }] — calls [_extraire<Object?>(...)] without using its result: The server returns [Reponse.ok(null)] for this route, so there is nothing more specific to specify—the same choice as [extraire<null>(reponseHttp)] on the [Vue.js] side.

docs.title: 5.7.1. lib/core/http/auth_http_client.dart
docs.text:
Port of [core/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts]: adds the token [JWT] to every protected request, logs the user out on a 401 response.

// =========================================================================
// core/http/auth_http_client.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts (client Vue.js of this
// course). This file does two things, just like its counterpart
// Vue.js (itself a port of the Angular and React clients):
// 1. adds the "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header to every request, if
// the user is logged in (see AuthService.accessToken);
// 2. if the server returns a 401 response (token missing, invalid, or expired),
// gracefully log the user out on the client side.
//
// [fetch] (used in Vue.js and React) and Angular’s [HttpClient] have
// no equivalent to DIRECT in Dart: the [http] package (see pubspec.yaml)
// provides free functions (http.get(...), http.post(...)) rather
// than an object to be intercepted globally. The port remains faithful, however,
// in ESPRIT to useAuthFetch(): rather than a composable function returning
// an “enriched fetch,” here we write a VRAIE CLASSE, [AuthHttpClient],
// whose get(...)/post(...) methods play exactly the same role—
// any code that wants to communicate with the server (here, only
// core/services/rdv_service.dart) calls the CES methods rather than the
// http package directly.
//
// Writing a class rather than a composable function is a natural choice
// in Dart/Flutter: unlike a <script setup> Vue.js (which
// runs only once per component instance; see the comment by
// auth.interceptor.ts), a ChangeNotifier or a Dart service class
// has no “body executed on every render” that you need to be wary of—
// so no equivalent of useCallback() is needed here either,
// but for a different reason: there simply isn’t a
// "function recreated on every render" to begin with, since the class is
// constructed only once by lib/main.dart (see below).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:async' show unawaited;

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../services/auth_service.dart';

class AuthHttpClient {
  final AuthService auth;
  final http.Client _client = http.Client();

  AuthHttpClient(this.auth);

  Future<http.Response> get(Uri url) => _envoyer(() => _client.get(url, headers: _entetes()));

  Future<http.Response> post(Uri url, {required Object body}) => _envoyer(
        () => _client.post(
          url,
          headers: {..._entetes(), 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
          body: body,
        ),
      );

  // constructs the headers common to all protected requests—the equivalent
  // of the "new Headers(options.headers); if (auth.accessToken) {...}" on the
  // Vue.js, but in the form of a simple Map<String, String> (the type
  // expected by the http package, which is simpler here than a Headers class).
  Map<String, String> _entetes() {
    final accessToken = auth.accessToken;
    return accessToken == null ? {} : {'Authorization': 'Bearer $accessToken'};
  }

  // extracts what get(...) and post(...) have in common: executing the call
  // HTTP and then, if the response is 401, log the user out—the
  // function [appel] passed as a parameter acts as the "...options"
  // sent by `fetch(path, { ...options, headers: headers })` on the
  // Vue.js: at this point, it is not yet known whether this is a GET
  // or a POST; we just need to execute it and then examine its response.
  Future<http.Response> _envoyer(Future<http.Response> Function() appel) async {
    final reponse = await appel();
    //: A 401 error during a session means the token is no longer valid
    // (expired, or server restarted): the client is gracefully disconnected
    // rather than leaving the application in an inconsistent state (apparently connected
    // on the surface, but where no requests are successful anymore). We do not
    // an "await" on seDeconnecter(): the response HTTP (even if it’s an error)
    // must be returned to the caller without waiting for the local storage purge to finish
    // local storage, which completes on its own in the background.
    if (reponse.statusCode == 401) {
      unawaited(auth.seDeconnecter());
    }
    return reponse;
  }
}

Let's comment on this code:

  • Lines 12–31: The header comment explains the choice of CLASSE ([AuthHttpClient]) over a composable—[fetch] ([Vue.js]/[React]) and [HttpClient] ([Angular]) have no direct equivalent in [Dart]; the [http] package provides standalone functions rather than a single object to be intercepted globally.
  • lines 46–54: [get(...)]/[post(...)]—the only two methods that [rdv_service.dart] calls; it never calls the [http] package directly.
  • Lines 60–63: [_entetes()] — constructs [{'Authorization': 'Bearer $accessToken'}] if the user is logged in; this is the equivalent of [new Headers(options.headers); if (auth.accessToken) {...}] on the [Vue.js] side, but in the form of a simple [Map<String, String>].
  • Lines 71–84: [_envoyer(appel)] — factors out what [get(...)] and [post(...)] have in common; [unawaited(auth.seDeconnecter())] documents EXPLICITEMENT, indicating that we choose not to wait for [Future] — the response HTTP (even if it contains an error) must be returned to the caller without waiting for the local storage purge to complete.

docs.title: 5.8.1. lib/core/i18n/translations_service.dart
docs.text:
Port FUSIONNÉ from [src/i18n.ts] ET from [core/composables/language.composable.ts]: the French/English interface switching, reimplemented without a third-party library (see the header comment in the file for the reason behind this choice).

// =========================================================================
// core/i18n/translations_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Porting FUSIONNÉ from src/i18n.ts (view-i18n configuration) ET from
// core/composables/language.composable.ts (Vue.js client from this course).
// Vue.js separates the two because vue-i18n, a third-party library already
// rich in features (pluralization, date/number formats...),
// handles all the actual translation work; language.composable.ts
// simply adds the ability to save the language selection in
// localStorage. Flutter does not have a direct equivalent to vue-i18n/react-
// i18next/@ngx-translate/core installed by default: rather than adding
// an additional dependency, this file reimplements in just a few
// lines—the subset used in this course: a
// dictionary with pointer keys ("LOGIN.TITLE") and a function t(key).
//
// DIFFÉRENCE DE PLATEFORME IMPORTANTE (see also the chapter “Porting
// the application to mobile, desktop, and web"): src/i18n.ts fetches
// each dictionary via a fetch("/i18n/{language}.json")—a URL
// relative URL, which assumes a SERVEUR WEB server serving the client files
// (Currently under development; a static server will be used once it is built). A
// Flutter mobile or desktop application has no PAS DE SERVEUR WEB to serve it
//: the code ET and its static resources (in this case, the files JSON) are
// EMBARQUÉS together in a single package installed on the device (.apk,
//.app, .exe...). This is why this file uses rootBundle.loadString(...)
// — the API Flutter component that reads a file specified in the [assets] section of
// pubspec.yaml directly from this package—rather than via a network call.
// On the web target, rootBundle relies behind the scenes on an actual request
// HTTP to the files published alongside the application, but this detail
// remains invisible here: the MÊME Dart code runs without any
// platform, across all three environments—which is precisely the central argument of
// this chapter.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart' show rootBundle;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const String _cleStockage = 'rdvmedecins.langue';
const String _langueParDefaut = 'fr';

class TranslationsService extends ChangeNotifier {
  String langueCourante = _langueParDefaut;

  // dictionaries that have already been loaded (avoids re-reading an asset file that has already been read
  // during the session)—same optimization as dictionnairesCharges on the
  // Vue.js (src/i18n.ts), but here the dictionary is stored directly
  // decoded rather than a simple Set of previously seen languages: Vue.js could
  // have been limited to a set because vue-i18n keeps LUI-MÊME the dictionaries
  // loaded into memory (setLocaleMessage); since there is no equivalent library
  // equivalent library here, this caching role must be handled directly by this
  // file.
  final Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> _dictionnaires = {};

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // to be called UNE SEULE times, in lib/main.dart, AVANT runApp(...):
  // restores the language saved during a previous launch (if any
  // one) and loads its dictionary—equivalent to the end block of
  // creerLanguageStore() on the Vue.js side (reading langueMemorisee in
  // localStorage), but made explicitly asynchronous for the same
  // reasons already documented in core/services/auth_service.dart
  // (shared_preferences is asynchronous, unlike
  // localStorage).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> init() async {
    String langueDepart = _langueParDefaut;
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      langueDepart = prefs.getString(_cleStockage) ?? _langueParDefaut;
    } catch (_) {
      // no readable preference: it starts in French, like
      // Vue.js (locale: 'fr' in createI18n({...})).
    }
    await _chargerDictionnaire(langueDepart);
    langueCourante = langueDepart;
    // No notifyListeners() here, for the same reason as in
    // AuthService.init(): this method is awaited before
    // runApp(...), so no widget is listening to this ChangeNotifier yet.
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: changerLangue(language) on the Vue.js side (triggered by the
  // FR/EN buttons in lib/app.dart; see later in this chapter).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> changerLangue(String langue) async {
    if (langue == langueCourante) {
      return;
    }
    await _chargerDictionnaire(langue);
    langueCourante = langue;
    notifyListeners(); // Here, however, the application is already running: a notification is indeed sent
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.setString(_cleStockage, langue);
    } catch (_) {
      // the language change remains in effect for this execution even if
      // the save operation fails—only a future restart would be affected.
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent to: chargerDictionnaire(language) on the Vue.js side—even
  // caching principle (dictionnairesCharges), but reading an asset
  // embedded asset rather than a network fetch() (see the header of this file).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> _chargerDictionnaire(String langue) async {
    if (_dictionnaires.containsKey(langue)) {
      return; // already loaded during a previous language change
    }
    final contenu = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/$langue.json');
    _dictionnaires[langue] = jsonDecode(contenu) as Map<String, dynamic>;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // the translation function itself—called t('LOGIN.TITLE') from
  // the widgets (see lib/features/...), exactly like t('LOGIN.TITLE')
  // on the Vue.js side (useI18n().t). The key is "separated by a dot" (a dot separates
  // each level): we therefore descend through the nested dictionary JSON one
  // segment at a time, rather than flattening the dictionary once and for all
  // for all of them, as vue-i18n does internally—a choice that remains
  // more than sufficient for the size of these two dictionaries.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  String t(String cle) {
    final dictionnaire = _dictionnaires[langueCourante];
    if (dictionnaire == null) {
      return cle; // Dictionary not yet loaded: display the key itself as a last resort
    }
    dynamic valeurCourante = dictionnaire;
    for (final segment in cle.split('.')) {
      if (valeurCourante is Map<String, dynamic> && valeurCourante.containsKey(segment)) {
        valeurCourante = valeurCourante[segment];
      } else {
        return cle; // key not found: same fallback as above
      }
    }
    return valeurCourante is String ? valeurCourante : cle;
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 16–31: The header comment details the most important part of this entire client: DIFFÉRENCE, DE, and PLATEFORME — [src/i18n.ts] retrieves each dictionary via [fetch("/i18n/{langue}.json")], a URL that relies on a SERVEUR and WEB; a mobile or desktop application does not have one, hence [rootBundle.loadString(...)] rather than a network call—the same code works, regardless of platform, on all three environments (see Chapter 5).
  • lines 66–80: [init()] — restores the saved language (or French by default) and loads its dictionary; Like [AuthService.init()], there is no [notifyListeners()] here (no widget is listening to this [ChangeNotifier] at this stage).
  • lines 107–113: [_chargerDictionnaire(langue)] — the same caching principle as [dictionnairesCharges] on the [Vue.js] side, but it directly stores the decoded dictionary rather than a simple [Set] of previously seen languages: [vue-i18n] kept the dictionaries in memory ([setLocaleMessage]); here, this caching role must be handled directly by this file.
  • Lines 124–138: [String t(String cle) { ... }] — traverses the nested dictionary JSON one segment at a time ([cle.split('.')]), rather than flattening the dictionary once and for all as [vue-i18n] does internally—a choice that is more than sufficient for the size of these two dictionaries.

docs.title: 5.9.1. lib/features/login/login_page.dart
docs.text:
Porting [src/app/features/login/Login.vue]: the login screen.

// =========================================================================
// features/login/login_page.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/login/Login.vue (Vue.js client from this course):
// the login screen. Like its counterpart Vue.js, this widget does not
// knows nothing about the calendar or appointments: it simply collects a
// pair (username, password), forward it to AuthService.seConnecter(...),
// and display any errors that may occur.
//
// DIFFÉRENCE STRUCTURELLE with Vue.js: Login.vue reports its local status
// (login, password, enCours, error) with simple ref(...) - Vue.js
//then automatically “redraws” the <template> when one of these refs
// changes, SANS concept of “stateful vs. stateless widgets.” Flutter explicitly distinguishes
// explicitly distinguishes between two types of widgets: StatelessWidget (nothing ever changes
// after construction) and StatefulWidget (has a mutable state,
// and can redraw itself via setState(...)). This component needs to
// to remember what the user types ET and to be able to redraw itself when
// enCours/error conditions change: it is therefore a StatefulWidget—the class
// LoginPage below simply calls QUE to declare createState(), while all the state and
// all the logic reside in _LoginPageState, the associated “twin” class
// associated with it.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/services/auth_service.dart';

class LoginPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const LoginPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const _LoginForm();
  }
}

class _LoginForm extends StatefulWidget {
  const _LoginForm();

  @override
  State<_LoginForm> createState() => _LoginFormState();
}

class _LoginFormState extends State<_LoginForm> {
  // TextEditingController: unlike v-model="login" on the Vue.js side
  // (which directly links a field to a ref, in both directions, with a
  // single attribute), Flutter does not have built-in two-way binding
  // for the TextField widget—you must explicitly have a controller, the
  // read (controller.text) and the LIBÉRER (dispose()) once the widget
  // has been destroyed; see dispose() below. It’s more verbose to write once,
  // but makes the lifecycle explicit (creation -> reading -> freeing
  // of resources) that Vue.js manages itself behind the scenes for a ref.
  final TextEditingController _loginController = TextEditingController();
  final TextEditingController _passwordController = TextEditingController();

  bool _enCours = false;
  String? _erreur;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    // frees the resources associated with the controls—an oversight here
    // would cause a memory leak every time this screen is
    // recreated. Vue.js, whose ref() are simple JavaScript objects
    // collected by the garbage collector just like any other object,
    // does not have to account for this step.
    _loginController.dispose();
    _passwordController.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  Future<void> _onValider() async {
    final login = _loginController.text.trim();
    final password = _passwordController.text;
    if (login.isEmpty || password.isEmpty) {
      return;
    }
    setState(() {
      _erreur = null;
      _enCours = true;
    });
    try {
      // context.read<AuthService>() : "one-time" read, SANS resubscription
      // to future changes (unlike context.watch<...>(), see
      // lib/app.dart) — specifically designed for a one-time call triggered by
      // a user action, rather than a view that needs to be
      // kept up to date. This is the Flutter/provider equivalent of
      // "const auth = useAuth();" alongside Vue.js, where auth.seConnecter(...) is
      // simply called without any specific distinction (Vue.js does not have
      // this distinction between one-time read and resubscription: useAuth() returns
      // always the same reactive object, regardless of how it is used).
      await context.read<AuthService>().seConnecter(login, password);
      if (!mounted) return; // the widget may have been destroyed while waiting for the server
      setState(() => _enCours = false);
    } catch (_) {
      if (!mounted) return;
      setState(() {
        _enCours = false;
        _erreur = 'LOGIN.ERROR';
      });
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // context.watch<TranslationsService>() : unlike
    // context.read<AuthService>() used in _onValider() above,
    // we want ICI this widget to automatically redraw itself if the language
    // changes (FR/EN buttons in lib/app.dart)—watch() subscribes to
    // future changes, whereas read() simply performs a one-time read.
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;

    return Center(
      child: ConstrainedBox(
        constraints: const BoxConstraints(maxWidth: 420),
        child: Card(
          child: Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(24),
            // Form groups the fields together and allows validation by pressing
            // "Enter" from any of them (onFieldSubmitted
            // below)—the equivalent of the <form @submit.prevent="onValider">
            // from Login.vue: Entering text into a ET field and clicking the button
            // both trigger the same onValider().
            child: Column(
              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
              children: [
                Text(t('LOGIN.TITLE'), style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge),
                const SizedBox(height: 16),
                if (_erreur != null) ...[
                  Container(
                    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
                    decoration: BoxDecoration(
                      color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.errorContainer,
                      borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(4),
                    ),
                    child: Text(
                      t(_erreur!),
                      style: TextStyle(color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onErrorContainer),
                    ),
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 16),
                ],
                TextField(
                  controller: _loginController,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL')),
                  textInputAction: TextInputAction.next,
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 12),
                TextField(
                  controller: _passwordController,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL')),
                  obscureText: true,
                  textInputAction: TextInputAction.done,
                  // onSubmitted: triggered by the “Enter” key (or its
                  // mobile virtual keyboard equivalent)—the counterpart to
                  // @submit.prevent placed on the <form> tag on the Vue.js side,
                  // placed here directly on the DERNIER form field.
                  onSubmitted: (_) => _onValider(),
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 20),
                FilledButton(
                  onPressed: _enCours ? null : _onValider,
                  child: Text(_enCours ? t('LOGIN.SUBMITTING') : t('LOGIN.SUBMIT')),
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 16),
                Text(
                  '${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_PREFIX')} admin / admin ${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ADMIN')} '
                  '${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_OR')} user / user ${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_USER')}.',
                  style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodySmall,
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 39–44: [LoginPage] (a simple front-end for [StatelessWidget]) delegates TOUT to [_LoginForm]/[_LoginFormState] — the header comment explains why this screen, which must store what the user types into ET, redraws itself when [enCours]/[erreur] change, PAS cannot simply be [StatelessWidget], unlike [Login.vue], where [ref(...)] makes no such distinction.
  • lines 55–56: [final TextEditingController _loginController = TextEditingController();] — replaces [v-model="login"]: no built-in bidirectional link in [TextField]; a controller must be explicitly specified.
  • lines 61–71: [dispose() { _loginController.dispose(); _passwordController.dispose(); ... }] — releases both controllers; an omission here would cause a memory leak every time this screen is recreated, a step that [Vue.js] does not need to account for (its [ref()] objects are simply collected by the garbage collector).
  • lines 93–102: [await context.read<AuthService>().seConnecter(login, password);] within a [try/catch] — [context.read<...>()] (one-time read, SANS resubscription) rather than [context.watch<...>()] (see [lib/app.dart]), which is well-suited for a one-time call triggered by a user action.
  • Line 160: [onSubmitted: (_) => _onValider(),] placed on the DERNIER field (password) — the counterpart to [@submit.prevent="onValider"], which is set on the [<form>] tag, which in turn is set on the [Vue.js] field: Entering a ET field and clicking the button triggers both the same [_onValider()].

docs.text:
Porting of [src/app/features/doctor-day-picker/DoctorDayPicker.vue]: Select a doctor and a date, then request to view their schedule.

// =========================================================================
// features/doctor_day_picker/doctor_day_picker.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Porting of src/app/features/doctor-day-picker/DoctorDayPicker.vue (client
// Vue.js for this course): the widget that lets you choose a doctor and a
// date, and then view their schedule.
//
// A [defineProps]/[defineEmits] Vue.js (input props, output events
// output) becomes, quite simply, a CONSTRUCTEUR Dart: the props
// are the named constructor parameters (doctors, onRechercher), and
// "emit an event" simply becomes APPELER the function received as a
// parameter—exactly the choice already made by the React client of this
// course (a `function` prop, onRechercher), rather than the
// explicit declaration [defineEmits] specific to Vue.js. Flutter, like React, does not
// AUCUNE syntactic distinction between a “normal prop” and a “prop used to
// notify the parent": it’s a function like any other, passed via the
// parent (see lib/app.dart) when this widget is constructed.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/rdv_models.dart';

// "yyyy-MM-dd" format—the same date format as on the Vue.js
// (new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)), but constructed explicitly here
// using the intl package rather than string slicing: DateTime from Dart
// does not have a built-in toISOString() method.
final DateFormat _formatJour = DateFormat('yyyy-MM-dd');

class DoctorDayPicker extends StatefulWidget {
  final List<Medecin> medecins;

  // onRechercher(idMedecin, day): the direct equivalent of
  // "search: [criteres: { idMedecin: number; jour: string }]" on the
  // Vue.js—here, two positional parameters rather than a single object
  // {idMedecin, day}, one choice being just as valid as the other in Dart.
  final void Function(int idMedecin, String jour) onRechercher;

  const DoctorDayPicker({super.key, required this.medecins, required this.onRechercher});

  @override
  State<DoctorDayPicker> createState() => _DoctorDayPickerState();
}

class _DoctorDayPickerState extends State<DoctorDayPicker> {
  // state that is purely local to this widget (what is selected in the menus,
  // as long as the user hasn’t clicked the button) — the equivalent
  // direct equivalent of idMedecinSelectionne/jourSelectionne on the Vue.js side, in the form of
  // simple fields from _DoctorDayPickerState rather than ref(...): a
  // StatefulWidget Flutter doesn’t require any special “wrapping” for
  // a local field; setState(...) (see _onChoixMedecin below) is sufficient to
  // indicate that a redraw is needed.
  int? _idMedecinSelectionne;
  DateTime _jourSelectionne = DateTime.now();

  Future<void> _choisirJour() async {
    // Flutter does not have a direct equivalent for <input type="date"> (a
    // date input widget NATIF DU NAVIGATEUR, such as Vue.js could
    // on the web side): across the three environments targeted by this client
    // (mobile, desktop, web), it is Flutter LUI-MÊME that renders the
    // date picker (showDatePicker(...) shown below)—a
    // Material widget, identical in appearance across all three targets. This is a
    // very concrete illustration of the promise “one code for three
    // environments”: whereas Vue.js relied on a component from the
    // browser (which is missing on mobile and desktop), Flutter provides its
    // own component, available at PARTOUT.
    final choisi = await showDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _jourSelectionne,
      firstDate: DateTime(2020),
      lastDate: DateTime(2100),
    );
    if (choisi != null) {
      setState(() => _jourSelectionne = choisi);
    }
  }

  void _onClicRechercher() {
    final idMedecin = _idMedecinSelectionne;
    if (idMedecin == null) {
      return; // the button is disabled in this case anyway (see build() below)
    }
    // widget.onRechercher(...): we call the function received from the parent—
    // exactly equivalent to emit('search', ...) on the Vue.js side, or to
    // calling the prop onRechercher(...) on the React side. The "widget." prefix
    // is required here because _DoctorDayPickerState is a class
    // SÉPARÉE of DoctorDayPicker (see the header in lib/features/login/login_page.dart
    // due to this Flutter-specific State/Widget separation):
    // this is how, from the state, we access the parameters of the widget that
    // that owns it.
    widget.onRechercher(idMedecin, _formatJour.format(_jourSelectionne));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;

    // The three fields are constructed here as UNE, SEULE, and FOIS, then arranged by
    // the LayoutBuilder lower section: side by side (Row) on a wide screen,
    // stacked (Column) on a narrow screen. A phone in portrait mode is
    // only about 360 pixels wide: three fields in a row would each fit
    // only about 100 pixels each and would overflow.
    //
    // DropdownButtonFormField<int>: the Flutter equivalent of a
    // <select> HTML—unlike v-model="idMedecinSelectionne"
    // on the Vue.js side (a single two-way binding), Flutter
    // explicitly separates "displayed value" (value:) and "reaction
    // to a change" (onChanged:), similar to React
    // (:value + @change) already compared in the original .vue
    //.
    final champMedecin = DropdownButtonFormField<int>(
      // isExpanded: the label takes up the entire available width (and is
      // neatly truncated if it’s too long) instead of overflowing.
      isExpanded: true,
      decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL')),
      value: _idMedecinSelectionne,
      hint: Text(t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR')),
      // .map(...).toList() : the Flutter equivalent of
      // v-for="doctor in doctors":key="medecin.id"—here,
      // the "stable" identifier (:key on the Vue.js side) is simply
      // the [value:] of each DropdownMenuItem (medecin.id), which
      // Flutter itself uses to determine which one is
      // is currently selected.
      items: widget.medecins
          .map(
            (medecin) => DropdownMenuItem(
              value: medecin.id,
              child: Text('${medecin.titre} ${medecin.prenom} ${medecin.nom}'),
            ),
          )
          .toList(),
      onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _idMedecinSelectionne = id),
    );

    // InkWell: makes the entire area “clickable”—a tap
    // anywhere on it opens the date picker
    // (_choisirJour above). This is a reconstruction, in the
    // manually, of what the browser used to offer “for free” with
    // <input type="date" v-model="jourSelectionne"> on the Vue.js side.
    // InputDecorator (rather than a “disguised” TextField) displays
    // the date without having a TextEditingController—there is
    // here—no RIEN to type in, just a value to
    // display and a tap to intercept: no need for the
    // create/dispose lifecycle already encountered in
    // lib/features/login/login_page.dart for a truly editable field.
    final champJour = InkWell(
      onTap: _choisirJour,
      child: InputDecorator(
        decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL')),
        child: Text(_formatJour.format(_jourSelectionne)),
      ),
    );

    final boutonAgenda = FilledButton(
      onPressed: _idMedecinSelectionne == null ? null : _onClicRechercher,
      child: Text(t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_AGENDA')),
    );

    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        // LayoutBuilder: calls its builder with the width RÉELLEMENT
        // available at this location in the tree (contraintes.maxWidth), and
        // recalls it if it changes (screen rotation, resizing
        // of the window)—so the layout adjusts automatically.
        child: LayoutBuilder(
          builder: (context, contraintes) {
            if (contraintes.maxWidth < 600) {
              return Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
                children: [
                  champMedecin,
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  champJour,
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  boutonAgenda,
                ],
              );
            }
            return Row(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end,
              children: [
                Expanded(flex: 5, child: champMedecin),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
                Expanded(flex: 4, child: champJour),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
                Expanded(flex: 3, child: boutonAgenda),
              ],
            );
          },
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 59–79: [_choisirJour()] calls [showDatePicker(...)]—a very concrete illustration of the promise “a single code for three environments”: whereas [Vue.js] relied on [<input type="date">], a building block consisting of NATIVE, DU, and NAVIGATEUR (missing on mobile and desktop), [Flutter] renders LUI-MÊME—a selector that is a [Material] widget that is strictly identical across all three targets.
  • Lines 114–136: [DropdownButtonFormField<int>(value: _idMedecinSelectionne, ..., onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _idMedecinSelectionne = id))] — replaces [v-model="idMedecinSelectionne"] with an explicit pair [value:]/[onChanged:], similar to the pair [:value]/[@change] already encountered in connection with [React] in this course.
  • lines 149–155: [InkWell(onTap: _choisirJour, child: InputDecorator(...))] — manually reconstructed from what the browser provided “for free” with [<input type="date">]; [InputDecorator] (rather than a “disguised” [TextField]) displays the date SANS, which belongs to [TextEditingController].
  • Lines 169–194: [LayoutBuilder(builder: (context, contraintes) { ... })] — the response from [Flutter] to a screen of unknown width: [builder] receives the width actually available at that location ([contraintes.maxWidth]) and is called again if it changes (screen rotation, window resizing). Below 600 pixels—a phone in portrait mode is only about 360 pixels wide—the three fields are EMPILÉS within a [Column]; above that, they remain side by side within a [Row]. The three fields are constructed once, earlier on, in the variables [champMedecin], [champJour], and [boutonAgenda]: only their layout changes. With just the [Row] from the first version, each field would have had only about a hundred pixels on a phone in portrait mode, and the content would have overflowed (the yellow and black banner “RIGHT OVERFLOWED BY … PIXELS” in debug mode); [isExpanded: true] in the drop-down list prevents the same overflow for a long doctor’s name.

Port of [src/app/features/agenda/Agenda.vue]: a doctor’s schedule for a given day—available slots (“Book” button) or booked slots (patient + “Cancel” button).

// =========================================================================
// features/agenda/agenda_view.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/agenda/Agenda.vue (client Vue.js for this
// course): displays a doctor’s schedule for a given day—the list of
// their time slots, each of which is either available ("Book" button) or booked
// (patient’s name + “Cancel” button).
//
// Since authentication was added, this widget also receives
// peutModifier: when set to false (role USER), the “Book”/“Cancel” buttons
// disappear—the calendar remains viewable, but in read-only mode (the
// server would refuse these actions for a USER user anyway, returning a 403 Forbidden error,
// see RolesGuard on the server side).
//
// [v-if]/[v-else] and [v-for] (Vue.js) are converted back to Dart expressions here
// ORDINAIRES: Flutter, like React before it (see the comment on
// Agenda.vue), does not have a “template language” separate from the programming language
// programming language—const, if, for, and the ./?? operators in standard Dart
// are sufficient to express conditions and lists, directly within the
// build(...) method below.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/rdv_models.dart';

class AgendaView extends StatelessWidget {
  final AgendaMedecinJour? agenda;
  final bool peutModifier;
  final void Function(CreneauJson creneau) onReserver;
  final void Function(RvJson rv) onAnnuler;

  const AgendaView({
    super.key,
    required this.agenda,
    required this.peutModifier,
    required this.onReserver,
    required this.onAnnuler,
  });

  // a small formatting utility function that outputs "8:05" rather than "8:5"—
  // similar in concept to formaterHeure(...) on the Vue.js side.
  static String _formaterHeure(int h, int m) => '$h:${m.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';

  void _onClicCreneau(CreneauAgenda creneauAgenda) {
    if (!peutModifier) {
      return; // the button isn't displayed in this case anyway (see build() below)
    }
    final rv = creneauAgenda.rv;
    if (rv == null) {
      onReserver(creneauAgenda.creneau); // slot available: a reservation is offered
    } else {
      onAnnuler(rv); // slot already booked: the system suggests canceling the existing appointment
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;
    final agenda = this.agenda;

    if (agenda == null) {
      return Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 24),
        child: Text(
          t('AGENDA.EMPTY_STATE'),
          style: TextStyle(color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.outline),
        ),
      );
    }

    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Text(
              '${t('AGENDA.TITLE_PREFIX')} ${agenda.jour} - ${agenda.medecin.titre} '
              '${agenda.medecin.prenom} ${agenda.medecin.nom}',
              style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium,
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            // DataTable: the Flutter Material equivalent of <table> HTML from
            // Agenda.vue — unlike HTML, its lines must be
            // explicitly constructed in Dart using .map(...).toList()
            // (again, the equivalent of v-for="creneauAgenda" in
            // agenda.creneaux" :key="creneauAgenda.creneau.id" - DataRow
            // does not require an explicit "key" like Vue.js/React: the
            // list is completely rebuilt on every render; Flutter does not
            // does not attempt to reuse existing rows here).
            SingleChildScrollView(
              scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal,
              child: DataTable(
                columns: [
                  DataColumn(label: Text(t('AGENDA.COLUMN_SLOT'))),
                  DataColumn(label: Text(t('AGENDA.COLUMN_STATUS'))),
                  const DataColumn(label: Text('')),
                ],
                rows: agenda.creneaux.map((creneauAgenda) {
                  final rv = creneauAgenda.rv;
                  final creneau = creneauAgenda.creneau;
                  return DataRow(
                    // slightly tinted background for an available slot—the
                    // counterpart to the "free-slot" class on the Vue.js side.
                    color: rv == null
                        ? WidgetStateProperty.all(Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surfaceContainerLow)
                        : null,
                    cells: [
                      DataCell(Text(
                        '${_formaterHeure(creneau.hDebut, creneau.mDebut)} - '
                        '${_formaterHeure(creneau.hFin, creneau.mFin)}',
                      )),
                      DataCell(
                        rv == null
                            ? Chip(
                                label: Text(t('AGENDA.FREE')),
                                backgroundColor: Colors.green.shade100,
                              )
                            : Chip(
                                label: Text('${rv.client?.titre ?? ''} ${rv.client?.prenom ?? ''} ${rv.client?.nom ?? ''}'),
                              ),
                      ),
                      DataCell(
                        // peutModifier: false for a role USER (read-only)
                        peutModifier
                            ? OutlinedButton(
                                onPressed: () => _onClicCreneau(creneauAgenda),
                                child: Text(rv == null ? t('AGENDA.BOOK') : t('AGENDA.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT')),
                              )
                            : const SizedBox.shrink(),
                      ),
                    ],
                  );
                }).toList(),
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 43–57: [_formaterHeure(h, m)] and [_onClicCreneau(creneauAgenda)] — the latter distinguishes between an available slot ([onReserver(...)]) and a booked slot ([onAnnuler(...)]) depending on whether [creneauAgenda.rv] is [null] or not, exactly the same logic as on the [Vue.js] side, but expressed purely in [Dart] rather than in [<template>].
  • Lines 96–137: [DataTable(columns: [...], rows: agenda.creneaux.map((creneauAgenda) { ... }).toList())] — the [Material] equivalent of [<table>] [HTML] from [Agenda.vue]: its lines must be explicitly constructed via [.map(...).toList()].
  • Lines 108–110: [color: rv == null ? WidgetStateProperty.all(Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surfaceContainerLow) : null,] — the counterpart to the [CSS] and ["creneau-libre"] classes on the [Vue.js] side: a background color applied conditionally to the entire line, here via a named function rather than a class named [CSS].

docs.text:
Porting of [src/app/features/booking-dialog/BookingDialog.vue]: a patient’s selection to reserve an available time slot—the file where the structural difference from [Vue.js] is most pronounced in this entire client.

// =========================================================================
// features/booking_dialog/booking_dialog.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Porting src/app/features/booking-dialog/BookingDialog.vue (client
// Vue.js for this course): the (modal) window that allows a
// patient to book an available time slot.
//
// DIFFÉRENCE STRUCTURELLE IMPORTANTE with Vue.js (and with the other three
// widgets from lib/features/): BookingDialog.vue is a component of TOUJOURS
// PRÉSENT in the tree, whose prop [ouvert] (a Boolean held by
// App.vue) controls the display (v-if="open")—EXACTEMENT the same
// choice as the Angular and React clients in this course, driven by the need
// to prevent Vue.js and Bootstrap’s JavaScript from competing for the
// same information (“Is the modal open?”).
//
// Flutter doesn’t have this problem: a dialog is NOT a widget
// that is conditionally shown or hidden in the tree, but a VRAIE
// PAGE, pushed onto the navigation stack (the Navigator) the moment
// it is opened, along with showDialog(...)—and automatically popped off the stack upon
// closing. Therefore, there is no NI “open: bool” state to maintain in the
// parent widget (see lib/app.dart, which has no field equivalent to
// creneauEnReservation on the Vue.js side), NI “confirm”/“close” events to
// send: showDialog(...) returns a Future that resolves with the
// value passed to Navigator.pop(...)—null if the user closed
// without making a selection; otherwise, the ID of the selected patient. This is the widget
// APPELANT (lib/app.dart) that waits for this Future using `await` to determine what
// to do next—a complete reversal of the direction of communication by
// compared to the two Vue.js events.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/rdv_models.dart';

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Help function: opens the dialog box and returns the ID of the
// selected patient (or null if the user canceled or closed without making a selection).
// This is the function that lib/app.dart calls—never call the
// the constructor of _BookingDialogContent below.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
Future<int?> ouvrirBookingDialog({
  required BuildContext context,
  required CreneauJson creneau,
  required List<Client> clients,
}) {
  return showDialog<int>(
    context: context,
    builder: (_) => _BookingDialogContent(creneau: creneau, clients: clients),
  );
}

class _BookingDialogContent extends StatefulWidget {
  final CreneauJson creneau;
  final List<Client> clients;

  const _BookingDialogContent({required this.creneau, required this.clients});

  @override
  State<_BookingDialogContent> createState() => _BookingDialogContentState();
}

class _BookingDialogContentState extends State<_BookingDialogContent> {
  int? _idClientSelectionne;

  void _onClicConfirmer() {
    final idClient = _idClientSelectionne;
    if (idClient == null) {
      return;
    }
    // Navigator.pop(context, idClient): closes the ET dialog box
    // passes idClient as the result of the Future returned by
    // ouvrirBookingDialog(...) — the equivalent, in a single call, of
    // emit('confirm', { idClient }) SUIVI for the closure (implicit,
    // controlled by the parent via [ouvert]) on the Vue.js side.
    Navigator.pop(context, idClient);
  }

  void _onClicFermer() {
    // Navigator.pop(context) without a second argument: the Future returned by
    // ouvrirBookingDialog(...) ends with null—the equivalent of
    // emit('close') on the Vue.js side.
    Navigator.pop(context);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;
    final creneau = widget.creneau;

    // AlertDialog: the Material widget dedicated to dialog boxes—
    // already provides, on its own, the darkened background (the equivalent of the
    // .modal-backdrop hard-coded in Vue.js) and the
    // standard closing behavior (tapping outside the dialog box, Esc key
    // on desktop/web)—a behavior that the client Vue.js had to
    // recreate on its own, as Bootstrap only handles part of it automatically.
    return AlertDialog(
      title: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE')),
      content: Column(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text(
            '${t('BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT_FROM')} ${creneau.hDebut}:${creneau.mDebut.toString().padLeft(2, '0')} '
            '${t('BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT_TO')} ${creneau.hFin}:${creneau.mFin.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}',
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          DropdownButtonFormField<int>(
            decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL')),
            value: _idClientSelectionne,
            hint: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT')),
            items: widget.clients
                .map(
                  (client) => DropdownMenuItem(
                    value: client.id,
                    child: Text('${client.titre} ${client.prenom} ${client.nom}'),
                  ),
                )
                .toList(),
            onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _idClientSelectionne = id),
          ),
        ],
      ),
      actions: [
        TextButton(onPressed: _onClicFermer, child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL'))),
        FilledButton(
          onPressed: _idClientSelectionne == null ? null : _onClicConfirmer,
          child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM')),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 16–28: The header comment summarizes the most significant structural difference in this file—[BookingDialog.vue] is a component of TOUJOURS and PRÉSENT in the tree, one of which has a Boolean property ([ouvert], held by [App.vue]) controls only the display; a dialog box [Flutter], on the other hand, is not present—JAMAIS—until it is explicitly opened with [showDialog(...)]—a true page stacked on the navigation stack, automatically unstacked when closed.
  • Lines 43–52: [Future<int?> ouvrirBookingDialog({...}) { return showDialog<int>(context: context, builder: (_) => _BookingDialogContent(...)); }]—the function called by [lib/app.dart]; its return type ([Future<int?>]) already indicates that ELLE will eventually return either the ID of the selected patient or [null].
  • Lines 67–77: [Navigator.pop(context, idClient);] — closes the ET dialog box and returns [idClient] as the result of [Future], which was returned by [ouvrirBookingDialog(...)] - the equivalent, in a single call, of what [emit('confirmer', { idClient })] and SUIVI—a parent-driven closure—did for ENSEMBLE on the [Vue.js] side.
  • Lines 80–84: [Navigator.pop(context);] without a second argument—[Future] then ends with [null], which is equivalent to [emit('fermer')] on the [Vue.js] side. It is [lib/app.dart] ([_onDemandeReservation(...)]) that processes [await] and [Future] and decides what to do depending on whether the result is [null] or not — a complete reversal of the communication direction compared to the two events Vue.js.

docs.title: 6. Chapter 5 - Porting the Flutter Application to Mobile, Desktop, and the Web
6.1. A Single Source Code, Multiple Compilation Targets
docs.text:
This is the core of this chapter and the raison d’être of this course variant: AUCUNE, as mentioned in Chapter 4 ([lib/], [pubspec.yaml], [assets/]) remains unchanged, regardless of the target selected. “Porting” the application here simply involves choosing a different COMMANDE, DE, or COMPILATION ([flutter run -d <cible>] or [flutter build <cible>])—never to write, duplicate, or adapt any widgets. This is very different from what a port would have required using the tools covered in the rest of this course: a [Vue.js]/[React]/[Angular] only runs NATIVEMENT in a browser—porting it to mobile requires a tool like TIERS ([Cordova]/[Capacitor], not used in this course) that packages it into a native wrapper containing, in reality, an embedded browser (a [WebView]): the code remains unchanged, but it is not a native executable, unlike what is produced here for mobile and desktop (see Chapter 3, “What Flutter Doesn’t Do” (EST PAS)).

The six targets ([Android], [iOS], [macOS], [Windows], [Linux], [web]) are enabled—PAR, DÉFAUT—in any project created with [flutter create] since [Flutter 3] (see Chapter 1) - No configuration is required on the project side to add one. The only differences from one target to another are: the native compilation tools installed on the development machine ([Xcode], [Visual Studio], [GTK]...), the exact command executed, and—for mobile only—a detailed network configuration described later in this chapter.

docs.title: 6.2. Web target
docs.text:
The target already used in Chapter 2 ([flutter run -d chrome]). Two commands are sufficient:

flutter run -d chrome              # development, with hot reload
flutter build web                  # production build, in build/web/

[flutter build web] generates a standalone [build/web/] file ([index.html], [JavaScript], or [WebAssembly] compiled, resources) - to be deployed on a static web server (IMPORTE, QUEL, [Nginx], [Apache], a simple [npx serve]....), exactly like the [dist/] file generated by [npm run build] on the [Vue.js]/[Vite] side. This build remains a [JavaScript] file served by a browser: it therefore continues to depend on a [NestJS] JOIGNABLE server from that browser, and thus on [app.enableCors()] (see [src/main.ts] on the server)—which is already active, with no changes required on the server side for this target.

One point to note specific to this target: the “URL on the server” field on the login screen (see [_ServerUrlField] in [lib/app.dart], Chapter 4) must then point to a ATTEIGNABLE address from the browser running the application—[http://localhost:8080] is acceptable as long as the [NestJS] server is running on the same MÊME machine as the browser.

docs.title: 6.3. Desktop Target
docs.text:
Three operating systems, three sets of native prerequisite tools (see Chapter 1), but [flutter] commands that are identical in form:

flutter run -d windows              # Windows—requires Visual Studio (C++ Desktop)
flutter run -d linux                # Linux - requires development packages GTK

flutter build macos                 # production build
flutter build windows
flutter build linux

This target does not require any special network configuration for AUCUN: a desktop application runs on the same machine as the user and accesses [http://localhost:8080] exactly as any other program installed on that machine would (the “URL server” field on the login screen allows you, as with other targets, to point to a remote server if necessary).
